label: Free 2.0
title: License format int2, P-256 keys and KMS signing
lede: Integral 2.0 adds the int2 license format with algorithm choice (Ed25519 or ECDSA P-256) and key ids, signer objects for KMS and HSM keys, and a migrate command for existing licenses. int1 licenses stay readable.

items.title: ECDSA P-256 keys and int2 licenses
items.text: Licenses now carry their algorithm in the header, so you can sign with Ed25519 or with ECDSA P-256, the curve KMS and HSM services support. Everything below runs offline.
items.codeTitle: Generate a P-256 key, issue, inspect and verify
items.code:
npx integral keygen --alg es256
npx integral issue --product my-app --plan pro --feature beta \
  --limit projects=100 --email kunde@example.ch --kid kms-2027 \
  --updates-until 2027-10-05 > license.txt
npx integral inspect "$(cat license.txt)"
npx integral verify "$(cat license.txt)" --public-key "$INTEGRAL_PUBLIC_KEY" --product my-app

items.title: Convert old licenses with integral migrate
items.text: int1 licenses stay valid in 2.x, and one command re-signs a whole file of them as int2 with the same id, plan and dates, so revocation lists and renewals still match.
items.codeTitle: Migrate a file of int1 licenses
items.code:
npx integral migrate --file licenses.txt --private-key-file integral-private.key > migrated.txt
npx integral inspect "$(cat migrated.txt)"
npx integral verify "$(cat migrated.txt)" --public-key "$(cat integral-public.key)"
items.outputTitle: Real output (licenses.txt held one int1 license, id lic_old1)

items.title: Key rotation with a key ring
items.text: Pass several public keys by key id and mix Ed25519 with P-256. Apps keep accepting old licenses while you issue new ones with the new key.

items.title: Sign with a KMS or HSM through a Signer
items.text: signLicense accepts a signer object instead of a private key string, so the key can stay inside your KMS. ecdsaDerToRaw converts the DER signatures that AWS KMS, Google KMS and similar services return.

note: Outputs were captured from the published @sweberdev/integral 2.0.0 on Node 22 with throwaway keys. Ready-made KMS adapters belong to Integral Pro and are not covered here.
